root_idea.summary: An opening or accessible way extended toward something, especially a way to water; the root also conveys directing, making apparent, and extending upward.
root_idea.development: The semantic development runs from access to water and a clear road or way to a prescribed religious way, while also including things projected or raised and objects directed toward a target.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb with a distinct religious-legislative use.
Quran-attested noun with a distinct religious-law meaning.
Quran-attested noun denoting a prescribed religious way or dispensation.
The Quranic plural active participle is presented under its singular citation form شَارِعٌ.

senses.definition: To prescribe or ordain a religious way, law, or command for people.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrences, the verb governs a religious matter: God prescribes religion, or people are described as prescribing a religious way for themselves.

senses.definition: A divinely prescribed religious law or way of belief and practice.
senses.usage_conditions: In 45:18, it denotes a prescribed religious way or ordinance to be followed; this is the religious sense of the word, distinct from its classical sense of a watering-place.

senses.definition: A prescribed religious way or dispensation assigned to a community.
senses.usage_conditions: In 5:48, it denotes a divinely assigned religious course, in a context allowing different communities to have distinct ordinances; the discussion also associates it with what is subject to variation or abrogation.

senses.definition: Surfacing visibly or appearing at the water’s surface, with heads raised or lowered as the fish come to drink.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural شُرَّعًا describes fish in the Sabbath narrative; authorities explain the precise head movement differently, but agree on conspicuous surfacing or approach toward the bank.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter water and drink, or to take water with the mouth; of livestock, to come to the watering-place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be a person, an animal, or livestock collectively; the expression also covers entering the water or drinking with the hands.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter upon, begin, or commence an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually construed with فِي for entering into an affair or undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To communicate with or open onto a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a door, entrance, or dwelling; the related transitive construction makes an entrance communicate with the road and may describe a projecting roof directed toward it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To point or direct a spear, spears, or a sword toward someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The direction is toward or in the direction of the intended target; a spear may also simply be described as pointing directly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become apparent or to make something apparent, manifest, or plain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a road, affair, case, or religion; the transitive use can mean making such a matter clear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring cattle or camels to a watering-place, or make them enter the water to drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transitive construction may describe watering animals without drawing water by a pulley or serving it in a trough.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take an easy way of performing an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic extension of making animals enter the water, applied to choosing an uncomplicated method rather than exerting oneself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slit and strip off an animal hide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The traditional descriptions specify cutting the hide between the hind legs or otherwise removing it without making a skin vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To loosen or undo a rope or its slip-knot and insert its two halves into the loop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized handling operation involving the doubled cord.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise or elevate a thing considerably.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general transitive use; the evidence does not restrict the object to a particular class.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put or make a sail for a ship or boat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is the vessel and the supplied construction uses شِرَاعٌ for the sail.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a hand into a vessel, or make part of the arm reach into the water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The latter expression is an elliptical or inverted construction concerning reaching into water during ablution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffice someone or give someone what suffices.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be a person or a thing that provides sufficient means.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a plant or herbage, to become fully grown and satisfy camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is associated with vegetation that provides enough nourishment for camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To originate, embrace, or follow one’s religious way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction يَشْتَرِعُ شِرْعَتَهُ describes adopting or pursuing a way of religion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A clear, plain, open track, road, or way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is originally a verbal noun and is applied as a name for a manifest route.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The divine way of religion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical religious extension of the clear road sense; it is treated as synonymous with شَرِيعَةٌ in the supplied evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sufficient, fitting, or of the sort one seeks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In expressions such as شَرْعُكَ, it can mean sufficient for you or suitable to what you seek, and is used with singular, dual, or plural referents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The like or equal of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used predicatively for things that are alike; the form can function with singular, dual, or plural reference.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The chords or strings of a lute.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective term for the strings of the بَرْبَط or lute.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The thong or strap of a sandal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension based on resemblance to a string or chord.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Equal or alike; of people, together as one sort in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In expressions for people being شَرَعٌ, the group is understood as entering or participating in the matter together; the form may function as singular or plural.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A custom.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a non-religious nominal use distinct from the Quranic religious-law sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sinew snare used to capture the birds called قَطًا.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized hunting implement; its plural is reported as شِرَعٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A string or slender chord, including one stretched on a bow or placed on a lute.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence gives several related applications to slender or stretched cords and distinguishes their collective and plural forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A roof or covering projecting over a doorway or other place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is explained as equivalent to سَقِيفَةٌ, including a roofed-over place or projecting shelter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relating to religion or law; religious, legal, or legitimate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective for conformity with religious law or legal legitimacy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Full-grown plant or herbage that satiates camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective botanical use referring to nourishing mature vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sail of a ship or boat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sail is a broad piece of cloth or matting raised on a mast or yard and moved by the wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The neck of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on the raised form of a ship’s sail; raising the شِرَاع means raising the camel’s neck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Extended and long, applied to a person’s nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative descriptive use based on extension or length.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Courageous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied as an adjective to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Good or excellent flax.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical or material use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong palm fibres suitable for sewing leather.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reference is to fibres at the base of palm branches whose thickness and prickles make them useful for leatherwork.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Courage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun describing courage as an attribute of a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A permanent watering-place, resort, descent, or way to water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is especially applied to a visible, lasting water source such as a river, rather than water drawn from a well by rope; it may also denote an access point or gap by which people or animals reach water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet for a spear or spearhead, meaning long or associated with the named maker Shurāʿ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence reports both an attributive derivation and a possible relation to شِرَاعٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long-necked, applied to a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The camel’s neck is compared with the height of a ship’s sail.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of the flax called شَرِيعٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized occupational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Entering water to drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This active-participle use is applied especially to camels; the plural forms include شُرَّعٌ and شُرُوعٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Entering into an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial extension of entering water, used with فِي for entering into a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Situated near, opening onto, or overlooking a road or other thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to houses or dwellings whose doors open onto a thoroughfare, and more generally to anything near or overlooking something; stars may be described as near setting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pointing directly toward a person or target, applied to spears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participle describes spears directed toward or facing the intended target.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A main, common, manifest, or thoroughfare road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used substantively or with طريقٌ for a road into which people commonly enter or which is conspicuous and open.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A learned person who practices what he knows and instructs others; by extension, a religious legislator or announcer of religious law.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is also applied as a title to the Prophet in this learned or law-announcing sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having an extended, elevated, and long nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical adjective describing the end of the nose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: High or lofty, applied to a house or tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied example is بَيْتٌ مُشَرَّعٌ.

cautions: The Quranic شُرَّعًا is presented under the singular active-participle citation form شَارِعٌ; its Quranic interpretation centers on visible surfacing, while the reported head position varies between authorities.
The Quranic religious meanings of شَرَعَ, شَرِيعَةٌ, and شِرْعَةٌ are kept separate from the broader classical watering-place, road, implement, anatomical, and figurative meanings.
